title: Palmer Road Sports Hub (Hampshire County Council on behalf of Arun District Council)
description:
This was undertaken by Hampshire County Council on behalf of Arun District Council: Arun District Council seeks to appoint a consultant to lead the design and consultancy services associated with of a new Sports Hub at Palmer Road Recreation Ground in Angmering. 
The council's Playing Pitch Strategy undertaken in 2019, identified the need to upgrade and improve the current provision of pitches and changing facilities. Alongside investment from the Football Foundation, Palmer Road Recreation Ground is redeveloped as a multi-sport hub with improved grass pitches, changing facilities and a new 3G pitch. title: Supply of Coach-Built Vehicles to Hampshire County Council
description:
Hampshire Transport Management (HTM) are awarding a contract for a turnkey solution for complete supply of vehicles, associated equipment and conversion services. 

This contract was awarded following a call for competition to shortlisted suppliers on the Crown Commercial Services' Vehicle Conversions DPS (reference number RM3814). 

The Goods and Services in scope of the contract include the following:
The Goods required are two coach-built vehicles to provide specialist transport for an Adults Health and Care service and its users. The service users will include those with various mobility requirements and specifically bariatric wheelchair users. The Supplier shall also supply the chassis for the coach build.

The Services required are conversion services (including any Installation Works required in respect of the modifications) to modify the vehicles to fit the specification published with the call-for-competition documents.

Each vehicle requires the following warranties:
• a minimum of 12 months in respect of any vehicle modification work(s) as part of the specialist coach-build;
• a manufacturer's warranty that warrants the vehicle/chassis supplied is free from defects for a minimum of 3 years from the date of delivery.

The initial period of this contract will run until the earlier of the date of Delivery and 20 November 2024. There is an option to extend up until the earlier of the date of Delivery and 20 August 2025.

HTM is the fleet provision business unit within Hampshire County Council, supplying, maintaining, and supporting the Council's mobility requirements. HTM has over 800 vehicles of varying types, as well as five workshop locations to maintain the fleet in-house.

title: Hampshire County Council Education Catering Allergen Portal
description:
Hampshire County Council's Education Catering service provide 378 primary schools and 19 secondary school in Hampshire with school meals. Approximately 3000 children of those who partake in school meals, have registered medical allergies. 

This requires a service of a GDPR compliant online platform for the safe management, creation and administration of special diet menus for pupils with allergies or intolerances that wish to eat a lunch meal at a primary school who's catering is managed by Education Catering.  

The system is used for parents to provide information to schools to upload onto the portal, in order that Education Catering can manage their menu planning and production to avoid allergen risks for those children.

Education Catering is to cease from the end of March 2026 and the school meals service will be outsourced, after which a central allergen portal will not be required. 

The contract has been awarded by way of a Single Tender Action to the incumbent provider.

title: Support and Maintenance for Swift / ICS (extension May  2025 - October 2025)
description:
An agreement was made in December 2017 to return the hosting of the ICS system from Hampshire Council to the Isle of Wight Council. ICS hosting was originally transferred to Hampshire County Council after the establishment of a strategic partnership between organisations including the provision of senior management for Isle of Wight children's services. This took place in 2012. In the intervening period the ICS/SWIFT product set was sold by Northgate to OLM.

A parallel procurement process had been undertaken with Hampshire County Council for a replacement ICS System, as originally, the Council was to be implementing the same new social care system in line with Hampshire County Council's programme timelines and these were delayed extensively due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The project has now been re-launched independently of Hampshire following the recent termination of the agreement between our respective Childrens Services departments. This is now being driven by a team of external consultants who are project managing, configuring and migrating data.

The additional requirement set out for support and maintenance of the integrated children's services case management system and associated licenses at the Isle of Wight Council with OLM for Swift and ICS will cover this period and allow some contingency and time to allow for decommissioning of the outgoing system and servers. (01 May 2025 - 31 October 2025).

The support and maintenance of the integrated children's services case management system and associated licenses is required to remain directly with the incumbent supplier whilst the implementation and system transition is undertaken. The Council has had to extend a number of times due to delays with the project for the replacement system.

The Isle of Wight Council observed a 10-day standstill period which expired at midnight on 25 November 2024.

title: Domestic Abuse needs assessment on 10-25 year olds in Hampshire County Council
description:
The Hampshire Domestic Abuse Safe Accommodation Needs Assessment (2021) identified that there is a lack of data available locally on adolescents engaged in domestic abuse either as victims and/or causing harm. In addition, the rapid literature review on child and adolescent to parent violence and abuse for the Domestic Abuse Commissioner's Office (2021) located at Review-Full-November-2021-Baker-and-Bonnick.pdf stated that parents experiencing abuse by an adolescent often feel high levels of shame and hopelessness, which can act as a barrier to help-seeking, leading to continued and often escalating abuse. Due to this type of abuse being particularly stigmatised and unrecognised, this social problem is challenging to measure and address respectively. Despite young people being referred to the locally commissioned domestic abuse services, uptake following referral has been challenging particularly for the 16-18 year old age group.
Request to quote was sought in September 2022 for chosen providers to quote for the provision of this service, the return date received 0 bids and the option to direct award the service was taken.

title: Support and Maintenance for Swift / ICS
description:
Provision of support and maintenance of the integrated children's services case management system and associated licenses at the Isle of Wight Council. Duration from 01 May 2023 - 31 October 2023. The services can be provided only by a particular economic operator for the following reason: absence of competition for technical reasons. An agreement was made in December 2017 to return the hosting of the ICS system from Hampshire Council to the Isle of Wight Council. ICS hosting was originally transferred to Hampshire County Council after the establishment of a strategic partnership between organisations including the provision of senior management for Isle of Wight children's services. This took place in 2012. In the intervening period the ICS/SWIFT product set was sold by Northgate to OLM.

A parallel procurement process has been undertaken with Hampshire County Council for a replacement ICS System. The Isle of Wight Council is required to be implementing the same new social care system in line with Hampshire County Council's programme timelines and these have been delayed extensively due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The Support and Maintenance contract of the integrated children's services case management system and associated licenses is required to remain directly with the incumbent supplier whilst the implementation and system transition is undertaken. The Council has had to extend a number of times due to delays with the project for the replacement system.

A VEAT notice was published on 16th March 2023 (2023/S 000-007699). This was followed by a 10-day standstill period which ended at midnight on 27th March 2023. The contract is intended to begin on 01 May 2023 until 31 October 2023.

title: Hampshire Advocacy Service
description:
The contracting authorities are seeking the provision of advocacy services to eligible individuals of all age ordinarily resident in the local authority of Hampshire County Council (HCC) and/or covered by the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Integrated Care Board (HIOW ICB) and/or Frimley Integrated Care Board (ICB).

Advocacy services support someone or act on behalf of an individual to represent their views, interests and wishes within formal processes, assessments, hearings and interactions with other groups and organisations on a range of subjects that affect them and their lives. An advocate should be independent from the involved parties and act with impartiality, facilitating self-advocation, as much as possible, for the person concerned.

The purpose of an advocate is to assist an individual to represent their views, ask questions, explain the options available without offering advice or an opinion and to assist the person to maintain their wellbeing, supporting them to have breaks or time to process information as required. An advocate should always assist without offering solutions or a bias and they should always help without judgement.

Hampshire County Council requires access to the XA Infrastructure Asset Management System in order to manage the carriageway (CW) and Footway (FW) data and use UKPMS functions to manage other inventory and condition data in line with published highways asset management guidance. 

Hampshire County Council requires a XAIS Annual Engineers Inspection (AEI) to be carried out on 50% of its Hierarchy Category 1 to 6 carriageway (CW) network over a one-year period. This is to be supplied loaded in the XA system. Hampshire County Council may consider purchase of XAIS iV condition data for its Hierarchy Category 1 to 3 footway.

title: ​​PCI_Lot_A_097​ ​​Whitehill and Bordon Transport Strategy​
description:
A call-off from ​Lot A​ of the Place, Connectivity & Infrastructure Professional Services Framework 2022-2026 (Published 4 March 2022). 

 

To develop a draft updated Transport Strategy for the area of Whitehill and Bordon due to the extensive redevelopment in the area. • apply the principles and policies of the Hampshire Local Transport Plan (LTP4) • inform the priorities for the spend of the remaining s106 linked to the development The draft Transport Strategy will cover the whole area of Whitehill and Bordon and will take account of the views of local stakeholders, members, the developers and East Hampshire district council. It will identify local transport-related issues and problems and consider how these should be addressed. Work to develop the draft strategy and action plan will build upon existing work undertaken by Hampshire County Council, Whitehill & Bordon regeneration company and East Hants District Council, including their work on potential interventions. Council and WSP staff will work closely together throughout the project to share information and insight and to explore emerging ideas so that the resulting strategy follows good practice and reflects client expectations.

title: Work Out Your Money (WOYM) Financial Education for Adults
description: Work Out Your Money (WOYM) is a financial education initiative delivered by Citizen's Advice Havant, established in 2014. The objective is to change the community's perspective on money. Evidence shows people often only seek help when financial problems reach crisis point and that children learn money skills from their family, perpetuating poor money management across generations. Hampshire County Council wish to break this cycle so future generations have improved money skills. Debt and money is also often mentioned as a contributing factor in suicide, so this project aims to contribute to suicide prevention as per the Hampshire Suicide Prevention Plan. Similarly, addressing the mental wellbeing impact of cost of living pressures is a priority of the Hampshire Mental Wellbeing Strategy.

title: MEDIATION AND DISAGREEMENT RESOLUTION SERVICES
description:
Hampshire County Council has entered into contract for Mediation.  

The service will include a core service that supports mediation and

title: Adobe VIP Teams Licenses for HCC 2026-2029
description:
Hampshire County Council required access to industry-standard software to support the creation, editing and management of corporate documentation and visual content across its services. These tools are essential for producing professional, accessible and compliant materials that support operational delivery, communications and stakeholder engagement.
To maintain capability and ensure continuity of service, the Council undertook a procurement exercise for the provision of Adobe Acrobat Pro (VIPMP), Adobe InDesign (VIPMP), Adobe Creative Cloud Pro (VIP) and Adobe Photoshop (VIPMP) licences. These applications provide document production, graphic design and image editing functionality that is integral to the Council's day-to-day activities.
The procurement was conducted via the Government Commercial Agency Technology Products and Associated Services 2 (TePAS 2) Framework, Lot 3, providing a compliant and efficient route to market.
Objectives Achieved
The procurement exercise successfully:

Secured compliant and cost-effective licensing arrangements for the required Adobe products.
Ensured uninterrupted access to critical software for authorised users across the Council.
Supported the continued production of high-quality and accessible documentation and visual materials.
Enabled effective licence management through Adobe's Value Incentive Plan (VIP) and VIP Marketplace (VIPMP) programmes.
Maintained access to essential tools required for document creation, publication design and image editing, supporting operational and business needs across Council services.
Ensured continued alignment with existing business processes and software environments, minimising disruption to users and service delivery.

As a result, Hampshire County Council has maintained access to the software required to support its operational, communications and design functions while ensuring compliance, value for money and effective licence management.

title: Digital Bus Pass Solutions
description:
Hampshire County Council's School Transport service have procured a digital bus pass solution via a competitive quotation process. The aims and objectives of the service are to:

- To  ensure Hampshire County Council meets its statutory obligations to provide transport to eligible children on the vehicle that they  have been assigned.
-Enable monitoring of usage of vehicles and to ensure that vehicles are not overloaded or underutilised. 
- Improve the accuracy and timeliness of the data held by HCC on pupils accessing vehicles. 
-Ensuring the data that the Council has  on its pupils accessing services, is up to date.
- Improve the process, and reduce costs, for issuing bus passes by moving from hard copy bus passes to a predominantly digital solution.
-To work with a supplier that will support the implementation of an innovative solution to generate efficiencies and support the rollout to transport operators in line with the requirements detailed in the specification.
-Support the Council's environmental priorities by reducing the need to print and post paper bus passes to the addresses of eligible pupils and schools.

The contract duration will be one year with two optional one year extension options.

title: Lot 27 East Hampshire Younger Adults Supported Accommodation
description:
This contract will cover Younger Adults Supported Accommodation Services commissioned by Hampshire County Council. 

Younger Adults Supported Accommodation will have care and support attached to particular property.  This could be from a few hours a week to 24/7 support with a team of support staff. 

This Contract is initially for a capacity of 12 individuals.  The services are provided to 8 individuals in a block of 8 flats.  There are an additional 4 service users currently living in sole occupancy properties.  

There is likely to be future expansion of the Service if there is a requirement to support other individuals other properties in Hampshire. The Support Provider will be expected to work with the Council to help create Services that meet the needs of other individuals whose primary needs may fall within any of the client groups listed below. 

Client Groups 

The Client Groups that are eligible for these Services: 

People with a Learning Disability 

People with a Physical Disability/Sensory Impairment 

People with an enduring Mental Health condition 

People with Autism or Asperger's Syndrome 

At the point of tendering, the individuals identified have a learning disability.

The total value of the tender is worth up to £16,050,000 for up to 10 years, this includes the possibility of an expansion opportunity.  

The initial core service is worth up to £9,167,783 for up to 10 years. 

There may be scope for service expansion that will include another property(ies) and additional service users, worth up to £3,670,868 for up to 10 years. 

Awarded Value £8,427,648.60

title: PCI_LotA_054 Eastleigh Transport Strategy
description:
A call-off from Lot A of the Place, Connectivity & Infrastructure Professional Services Framework 2022-2026 (Published 4 March 2022).

To develop a draft transport strategy and area action plan for the Borough of Eastleigh which will: 
•	apply the principles and policies of the Hampshire Local Transport Plan (LTP4) 
•	inform the future development of the Eastleigh Local Plan 

The draft Eastleigh Transport Strategy will cover the whole of the borough and will take account of the views of local stakeholders and the public. It will identify local transport-related issues and problems and consider how these should be addressed. Crucially, it will set out practical measures that can assist in delivering local and national policies for the achievement of net zero emissions of greenhouse gases by 2050.  

Work to develop the draft strategy and action plan will build upon existing work undertaken by Hampshire County Council and Eastleigh Borough Council, including their work on potential interventions. It will also make use of the extensive database and analysis (the Evidence Base) that are available. Council and WSP staff will work closely together throughout the project to share information and insight and to explore emerging ideas so that the resulting strategy follows good practice and reflects client expectations.

title: Railway Bridge Project
description:
Hampshire County Council (HCC) own and maintain Havant Footbridge which crosses the railway at Havant in Hampshire. Whilst the footbridge is not part of the station infrastructure it is positioned within Network Rail (NR) land, with main span supports on the station platforms and access ramps within the forecourt and on NR non-operational land. Some sections are also within Havant Borough Council (HBC) land 

The footbridge was built in 1947 and provides the main public route over the railway. It connects the Civic Centre Campus, Havant College, and nearby large housing area of Leigh Park in the north to Havant Town Centre, Bus Station and Havant Park in the south. 

Deterioration of the footbridge has accelerated over recent years, and it is no longer deemed cost effective or practical to continue repairing it. In addition, the footbridge no longer meets uses needs. Therefore, the footbridge is to be removed, and a new one provided which meets current standards and provides access for all. 

Call off from Pagabo National Civils and Engineering Framework via Lot 2

description:

title: Provision of Water System Risk Assessments
description:
There are more than 700 buildings across the entire Hampshire Estate, most of them require their Legionella Risk Assessment and Schematic updating, together with written scheme implementation and any remedial actions arising to be reviewed and acted upon.   

The aim of the contract is to renew around 700 Legionella risk assessments and schematics which pre-date 2021, in line with the Hampshire County Council's Specification. The package of work will be spread over a 3-year period with approximately 200 legionella risk assessments and schematics completed every year. 

This contract was awarded via a further competition procedure on ESPO's Water System Risk Assessment and Water Hygiene Monitoring Services Framework (reference 198_20).

title: Inspection and Maintenance of Structures In and Around Watercourses 2024-2030 - AWARD
description:
Hampshire County Council (the Authority) is seeking to establish a single Contractor Term Service Contract for the Inspection and Maintenance of Structures In and Around Watercourses, to meet the Authority's statutory requirements to provide these works and services, particularly where they form part of the Highways network.  Delivery of inspection and maintenance works on watercourse structures are constrained by specific Health and Safety legislation. Where these works fall part of Highways infrastructure the requirements are specified under the Highways Act 1980.
      
      Full details of the Authorities requirements can be found in ITT Annex 1 Section 4 where the Scope and Specification is detailed. 
      
      The contract is valued at up to ?3.5 million and has an anticipated contract start date of 1st May 2024.  The initial contract period is 4 years to 30th April 2028 with an optional 2-year extension to 30th April 2030.  
      
      The proposed works under the contract will be split into two distinct tranches; each tranche will be delivered as follows:
      o Tranche 1 - the inspection regime, this is split over 2 years, with year 1 requiring a dive team of a minimum of 3 people; then year 2 made up of inspections in confined spaces or requiring robotic vehicles.
      o Tranche 2 - repairs and maintenance, is delivered by the Authority undertaking repairs and maintenance of Watercourse structures including planned maintenance activities. Contractors may be expected to undertake larger structural and Civil works on Highways infrastructure where the structure is within a Watercourse.
      
      It is expected this contract will have a wider use for the inspection and maintenance of structures that are either in or around a Watercourse, that do not fall part of the Highways infrastructure, example being canals and other Watercourse structures where the Authority has a duty to maintain.

title: Collaborative Assessment for the Management of Suicidality  (CAMS) Training
description:
The provision of Suicide Prevention Training to Hampshire County Council and partner organisation in line with the Hampshire and Isle of Wight (HIOW) Integrated Care System (ICS) footprint which targets frontline professionals and provides skills in managing one-off suicidal conversations, enabling people to signpost on to appropriate services. 

The training provided, provides a therapeutic framework and the  tools to work with a client on an ongoing basis in managing their suicidal ideation. This has been identified by partners as a gap, via local Suicide Prevention Forums and Partnerships across the ICS.

CAMS (Collaborative Assessment and Management of Suicidality) training is based on the work and research led by Dr. David Jobes and is based on suicide risk being treatable and works to address the drivers that make someone want to die by suicide.

title: Subject Access Request Support Services
description:
The Childrens Services directorate has established a  Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) to assist with the processing of outsourced Subject Access Requests (SARs) in the event of demand outweighing internal resource, ensuring statutory timescales can still be met. The requirement entails handling and processing of data regarding clients, customers, and members of the public, to enable the disclosure of information under the laws of UKGDPR and the Data Protection Act (2018).   

Services in scope of this requirement include:    
Provision of Subject Access Request disclosures within statutory timeframes stipulated in the UK GDPR. These timeframes will be given to the provider by the County Council.      

Ensure that responses provided to the County Council are accurate and that all information that is exempt from disclosure has been removed or marked for removal.   

Ensure that all information is secured to the appropriate security standards in transit and whilst being held in the provider's host system.   

The geographical scope of the services is limited to Hampshire County Council with the Children's directorate being the users of the DPS.  

The DPS will commence on the 26th March 2025 for a duration of 3 years. The DPS was procured under the restricted procedure -34(5) of the PCRs.

title: HCC Feb 2026 - The Provision of a Framework for the Supply of Cut Paper, Card and Envelopes - AWARD
description:
Hertfordshire County Council is currently out to procurement for the Provision of a Framework for the Supply of Cut Paper, Card and Envelopes.
      
      Hertfordshire County Council (HCC or the Contracting Authority) is leading on the procurement process to establish a Framework for the Supply of Cut Paper, Card and Envelopes. (hereinafter referred to as "Goods") and is seeking suitably qualified Suppliers to supply the Goods under any Framework resulting from this tendering exercise.  A list of the Goods required is given in the Pricing Schedule. You are invited to submit your tender for these Goods.  
      
      The requirement covers Cut Paper and Card and Envelopes to be delivered in bulk drops to the central stores of Herts Fullstop (trading department of Hertfordshire County Council). At Framework commencement, Hampshire County Council will be participating in Lot 4 only. Delivery will be to their central stores.
      
      The requirement is divided into the following Lots - 
      
      Lot 1	Branded Copier Paper
      Lot 2	Tinted Copier Paper & Card
      Lot 3	Whitebox Copier Paper
      Lot 4	Envelopes
      
      You are invited to bid for one or more Lots, or Lines within a Lot. 
      
      Full details are in the Specification, Schedule 1 of the Framework document.
      
      This procurement is an Open procedure.  Organisations wishing to take part in this project are invited to 'express an interest' and also 'opt in' which will give access to the full procurement documents in the e-tendering system.
      
      To be considered as a Tenderer you must complete and submit a Tender by the deadline of 12 noon on 8th April 2026.
      
      Please allow sufficient time to make your return, as Tender submissions cannot be uploaded and submitted after this return deadline. 
      
      Please ensure that where possible documents are uploaded as a PDF and that file names are succinct.  
      
      Any questions relating to this procurement must be made via correspondence on the website, in accordance with the procurement documents, and can be addressed to the main contact as shown in the details above.
      
      Tenderers should be aware that due to the nature of this requirement for Goods, any Framework formed as a result of this procurement process shall be executed as a deed. Tenderers should seek independent legal advice on the implications of this prior to submitting their Tender, where appropriate.
      
      Please note that the Framework requirements will be subject to available financial resources, supplier performance and flexibility to meet changing demands.
      
      Please ensure all your CDP information is up to date and you provide the most up to date CDP Share Code as part of your submission prior to the tender deadline. Share Codes provided after the deadline will not be able to be used and the Council will base the evaluation on the information submitted.
       
      To access this opportunity please visit https://in-tendhost.co.uk/supplyhertfordshire/aspx/Home

title: CP2279-22 Buy With Confidence Website and Administration
description:
This quotation is for creating a new public-facing website for the Buy With Confidence scheme (buywithconfidence.gov.uk), including ability for Buy With Confidence National team (which is hosted by Devon) to alter and update pages/composition at will.\r
\r
There is also a requirement for creating a new 'back-end' data management system/Customer Relationship Management (CRM) to hold data about the members of the Buy With Confidence scheme, as well as holding new applications to join the scheme, publicly submitted feedback about the members and complaints about them. The system will be accessible to 30+ local authorities, but data must be held securely in a way where they can only see information about the members/applicants in their own area (e.g. Hampshire County Council must only be able to see Hampshire based members), with only the Buy With Confidence National team, based in Devon, able to see all the data.\r
\r
The front-end website and back-end must be able to communicate to one another, for example, consumers can search for members of the scheme based on postcode and business type. People will also need to be able to leave feedback, complaints and make applications to the scheme, with the data held in the backend.\r
\r
There is a requirement for ongoing hosting, support and maintenance for the new website and data management system.

title: Provision of Restorative Justice Services for Hampshire and Isle of Wight - AWARD
description:
The Office of the Police Crime Commissioner for Hampshire and the Isle of Wight is seeking suitable qualified and experienced suppliers to tender for the provision of Restorative Justice Services across Hampshire and the Isle of Wight. 
      
      Restorative Justice brings those harmed by crime and those responsible for the harm into communication with each other. Restorative Justice offers victims an opportunity to be heard, to ask questions of the offender and to have their say in what they want to happen next. For some people who have been affected by crime, it can help them to explore why the crime happened. It can also help victims to move forward and feel less fearful of crime in the future. Evidence shows that people who take part in a Restorative Justice Process come away feeling satisfied because it has allowed them to have their say. Restorative Justice meets the needs of victims in a way that the traditional Criminal Justice System cannot.
      
      The Contract will commence on 1st April 2023 and will be for a period of 3 years with the option to extend for a further 2 years.
      
      Interested parties should register their interest in the project via the In-Tend website https://in-tendhost.co.uk/hampshire and complete and submit the tender return document together with any supporting information requested by 14.00hrs on Monday 21st November 2022.  
      
      How to obtain the Tender Documents
      The Tender documents can be accessed when logged into In-Tend by selecting 'View Details' on the relevant tender advert and clicking the 'Express Interest' tab. Once in the tender there are five tabs - 'Tender', 'ITT - documents', 'Correspondence', 'Clarifications' and 'History'. Select the 2nd tab 'ITT - documents' where you will find useful information under 'Tender Details' continue to scroll down to the heading 'Tender Documents Received' where you will be able to view / download the documents.
      
      Please download all the documents and read very carefully.
      
      Opting In and Opting Out
      Please note you are required to 'Opt In' before you can access the 'My tender Return' to start populating your response. 
      
      PLEASE NOTE you are required to 'Opt In' to view and complete the two Questionnaires for this project. 
      
      The 'Opt Out' functionality will also be available throughout the duration of the tender process. Opting out will give you the option of declaring you no longer want to receive any further communication in relation to this tender along with the opportunity of providing comments and feedback for this decision.
      
      You can choose to 'Opt In' at any time during the tender process if you initially decided to 'Opt Out'.
      
      Further Guidance
      In addition, guidance on how to participate in a tender - download and upload documents / returns and if required, register your company (free of charge), can be found on the In-tend site under the 'Help' or 'Information for Suppliers' buttons.

title: Professional Consultancy Services for the Enterprise M3 Local Enterprise
description:
This is award notice is published on behalf of The Enterprise M3 Local Enterprise Partnership.

Enterprise M3 Local Enterprise Partnership's are appointing a Professional Consultancy Services for the Enterprise M3 Local Enterprise Partnership's multi-site Enterprise Zone, in Hampshire and Surrey & have been supplied with the attached documents.

Enterprise M3 Local Enterprise Partnership (LEP) established a multi-site Enterprise Zone in April 2017 seeking to deliver 10,000 jobs and support 131 businesses. The Zone relates to three sites covering around 40 hectares in Hampshire and Surrey: 

i.	'Basing View' in Basingstoke, Hampshire; 
ii.	'Longcross Park' in Chertsey, Surrey and, 
iii.	Whitehill & Bordon in Hampshire. 

An initial 5-year Implementation Plan was developed and undertaken between 2017- 2022. Over £24 million of investment has delivered new infrastructure and enabled site development at each of the three Zone sites. With the completion of this initial investment period, Enterprise M3 LEP is seeking to commission multi-disciplinary consultancy support that will take the zone to the next stage of delivery and support partners in maximising the jobs, economic growth and business rates retained income over the remaining 20 years of EZ status.

The objective of the commission is to provide information and documentation that will inform and support the development of the second Implementation Plan that reflects the long-term objectives for the three sites, the key partners and the LEP.

This information will provide an evidence base for additional investment required across the multi-site Enterprise Zone. 

Since the information and Implementation Plan will be jointly owned by all parties engaged in this programme (Basingstoke and Deane Borough Council, East Hampshire District Council and Runnymede Borough Council) it will be essential for the Service Provider to engage fully with these parties throughout the contract period.

title: eBooks for Hampshire School Library Service
description:
Hampshire School Library Services (HSLS) is a sold service which provides advice and targeted stock selected by professional librarians to support learning in subscribing schools. It is among the most successful School Library Services in the country. 
As part of their subscription, schools have been able to access a range of children's eBooks via the HSLS platform and in addition buy titles through the same supplier for exclusive use by their own pupils. This is described as a 'hub and spoke model'. For the duration of their subscription, schools can access the HSLS stock contained in the 'hub' and retain ownership of any stock purchased direct through their own 'spoke' permanently. 

The objectives of this procurement were:

• To select a supplier who will provide a solution that is modern, easy to use and can age restrict eBook and eAudio titles to prevent access by pupils who are not of appropriate age

• To select a supplier who will provide access to a broad range of fiction and non-fiction titles aimed at children and young adults in various formats

• Include eResources (eMagazines and eComics) in the contract to enable schools to access all resources through one agreement

• To select a supplier who seeks to constantly improve the service available to HSLS and Schools


Please note, this is a Volume based contract up to £370,000 across the term length of the contract.

title: Hampshire De-Registration Partnership Register (HDPR 2023)
description:
The Hampshire De-Registration Partnership was established in 2015 with the 	aim of facilitating the de-registration of Care Home establishments for younger adults that were suitable for conversion to a model based on independent living.   

HDPR 2015 - 2022 - During the lifetime of the previous HDPR the County 	Council has worked with several Providers to look at de-registering their Residential Care Homes. To date 10 Residential Care Homes have been deregistered through this process. There have been a number of challenges which have impacted on the programme including engagement from Landlords, 	Provider Resource issues, variable responses from CQC and the pandemic. There remains an appetite from Providers to engage in deregistration of care 	homes. Having reviewed the current arrangements there are some changes that could be made that it is felt will assist the process and improve the outcome.  

This is a Multi-supplier light touch long term vehicle. We are targeting more than one de-registrations from suppliers which could take up to 10 years. This tender is being conducted in accordance with Chapter 3; Section 7 (Regulations 74/77) of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 (as amended). Providers are 	free to join the HDPR throughout the duration of the vehicle to commence the 	de-registration process

title: The Police and Crime Commissioner for Hampshire and Isle of Wight - Front Counter Refurb Works at Ryde, Totton and Yateley Police Stations
description:
Following the Pre-construction Services HP Contracts submitted their tender for the works which comprised:
Refurbishments of currently unused areas of their local police stations, to open these areas back up to the public. The sites have existing dated front counter facilities, and the aim is to provide light touch refurbishments of the areas within scope to allow for the local police stations to re-open to the public. These areas largely consist of a main reception area with glazed police enquiry counter and interview rooms, with most sites requiring refurbishment of further spaces adjacent to these areas such as small offices and accessible toilets. The current front counter areas have a condition commensurate to their use, age and time spent mothballed. At a high-level glance, all areas will require new decorations, wall finishes, doors, lighting, and minor amendments, alterations, and additions to existing M&E such as power and data. The front counter glazed screens are also to be upgraded to varying degrees.

External building fabric repairs (some at high/roof level) are required and include repair to roof finishes, timber resin repairs to windows, repointing, external joinery redecoration and the like.

New internal partitions and doors are to be installed to sub-divide the existing space and to suit client requirements with works including new floor & wall finishes throughout. Existing doors are to be improved to meet 30min fire standards.
A new mechanical ventilation system is to be installed, with further modifications to existing mechanical and electrical systems included - allowing for builders' works in connection with.
Additional smoke detection and directional signage is to be introduced, together with upgrading of the existing directional signage.
The property will be vacant during the course of the works.

title: Technical support for DPC project Hampshire Water Transfer and Water Recycling project
description:
Direct Award against the Government Commercial Agency (GCA) RM6309 Management Consultancy Framework Four (MCF4) - Lot 8: Infrastructure.

The Major Projects team is seeking to appoint a Technical Adviser ("Supplier") to support its work in the day-to-day delivery of the Hampshire Water Transfer and Water Recycling (HWTWR) project. 

By way of specific examples, the Services that we require are likely to include but are not limited to the following areas:
 
Provide assurance on technical feasibility including: 
• Engineering designs and treatment processes 
• Assets integration 
• Technical discreteness 

Assess project risk and delivery confidence including timelines/programme 
• Risk management and probabilistic modelling to test schedule and cost 
• Programme management and governance 
• Construction review and readiness and technical due diligence 

Review project management strategies including asset management 
• Project control and project management 
• Operational Readiness 
• Operational & Maintenance Strategy 

Review of procurement readiness and documentation for main contractors 
• Market engagement 
• Procurement and tendering strategy 
• Bid evaluation support 

Support planning and land acquisition strategy 
• Land acquisition strategy during planning 
• Support during planning 
• Advise on land acquisition, access rights, and associated risks

Continuity of expert advice will be a critical factor for the success of the work. 

Examples of other Deliverables include: 

• 	Ongoing assistance and advice with regards to the development of business cases, procurement strategy and technical aspects of the structuring of the scheme including supporting the client in meetings with the relevant company (as required). 
• 	Reports and assurance letters for our Board at key milestones, e.g. decision to go out for tender, decision to enter into contract with a Competitively Appointed Provider (CAP) etc. 
• 	General advice on technical matters when required. 
•	Review of formal and informal stage submissions.

title: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Health and Social Care Network
description:
NHS Hampshire and Isle of Wight Integrated Care Board (ICB) is awarding a 3 year contract to British Telecommunications (BT) Plc for 'Health & Social Care Network' (HSCN) Services. The contract provides network connectivity at circa 220 primary care and 2 data centres sites across HIOW. 

The contract is awarded via Lot 1: Data access services of the Crown Commercial Services (CCS) Network Services 2 Framework (RM808). The contact value  is £802,817.90 per annum, totalling £2,408,453.70 for the full three year period. The new contract will commence on 7th August 2023, and conclude on 6th August 2026,

The ICB have conducted a Direct Award process via Lot 1: Data access services of the Crown Commercial Services (CCS) Network Services 2 Framework (RM808). The ICB have conducted a desktop comparison exercise, as per the call off terms of the framework agreement, in order to establish which supplier provides the most economically advantageous solution. All of the service offers available under the relevant Lot were assessed and BT were selected as the successful supplier.

title: The Development To Passivhaus Plus Standard Of Six Apartments At Southbrook Cottages, Micheldever, Hampshire.
description:
Winchester City Council ("the Council") are committed through the 2020 - 2025 
Council Plan to the following key policies:  

• Tackling the climate emergency and creating a greener district 
• Homes for All: building homes that are energy efficient and affordable to run 
• Living Well: all residents to live healthy and fulfilled lives 

In support of the above, the Council are proposing a development of a 2 storey block of 6nr apartments together with associated site clearance, demolition of existing 
garages and sheds, hard and soft landscaping, drainage, external service 
connections and off-site car parking at Southbrook Cottages, Micheldever, 
Hampshire, SO21 3DJ.   

The Council are seeking to appoint a suitably qualified contractor with appropriate knowledge to build the apartments which are to be to the Passivhaus Plus standard. 
The Works are to be procured under the JCT Intermediate Building Contract with Contractor's Design, 2016 Edition (ICD 2016) using an open tender procurement 
process.  

It is anticipated that the development will commence on 28th November 2022 for a 
duration of 42 weeks.
